server-update.abort.login: The service restarted now at the owner's request and the sign-in was interrupted; sign in again
server-update.abort.restart: The service restarted now at the owner's request and this turn was interrupted: it was not replayed (nothing is redone by itself); send a message to continue if needed
server-update.abort.shell: The service restarted now at the owner's request and the command was ended (it may not have finished)
server-update.abort.stop: The service stopped and this turn was interrupted: it was not replayed (nothing is redone by itself); send a message to continue if needed
server-update.busy.online: work in the hands of {n} online AI(s)
server-update.failedBackFailed: {why}; rolling back failed too: npm install -g {pkg}
server-update.failedNoWayBack: {why}; there was no package to roll back to, so it was not rolled back: install a release that works again
server-update.failedRolledBack: {why}; rolled back to {own}, running as before
server-update.fetch.badVersion: The version {version} npm gave is not valid
server-update.fetch.dirUnreadable: The update source folder {dir} cannot be read: {why}
server-update.fetch.packUnreadable: The output of npm pack cannot be read
server-update.fetch.viewUnreadable: The output of npm view {spec} cannot be read
server-update.guard.exited: The new release exited after starting (exit code {code})
server-update.guard.noPreviousPackage: There is no package of the previous release
server-update.guard.noWayBack: {why}; there is no package of the previous release, so it cannot be rolled back
server-update.guard.notHealthyIn: It did not run properly within {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}}
server-update.guard.rollbackFailed: Rolling back to {from} failed ({why}); still running {own}
server-update.guard.stale: {to} was to be switched to, but {own} started
server-update.guard.staleUnmarked: {to} was to be switched to, but code without a release mark started
server-update.guard.tooManyStarts: It started {n, plural, one {# time} other {# times}} without running properly
server-update.guard.unhealthy: The new release did not run properly
server-update.keep.noTgz: Packing the running release failed: no tgz was made
server-update.keep.wrongRelease: The package made is {got}, not the running {release}
server-update.keepFailed: Could not keep a package to roll back to: {why}
server-update.noReleaseMark: The installed package has no release mark (.release)
server-update.noSource: No update source is set ({command} update --source <folder | .tgz | {example}>, or updateSource in runner.json)
server-update.noUpdater: This process has no updater attached (it is not a service started by the {command} command)
server-update.notGlobalInstall: Not installed globally with npm (a code checkout or another way): update it by hand where it is
server-update.notLocalTgz: {file} is not a .tgz file on this machine
server-update.notPackaged: This Daisy was not installed from npm and started by {command} start / start at login: it cannot update itself (update a code checkout by hand where it is)
server-update.notRestartable: This process does not come back by itself after exiting (no service manager, not a background process started by {command} start): it cannot switch releases. Stop it, npm install -g the new release where it is, then start it
server-update.package.badPackageJson: The package.json of {file} cannot be read
server-update.package.badVersion: The version {version} of {file} is not valid
server-update.package.changedWhileCopyin: {file} changed while it was copied; not taken
server-update.package.noGuard: The target release does not support safe update and rollback; install it by hand ({release}: no start guard; by hand: stop {product}, npm install -g {file}, start it again)
server-update.package.noRelease: {file} has no release mark (.release): it is not a Daisy package made by the packing script
server-update.package.notNpm: {file} is not an npm package (it has no package.json)
server-update.pendingUnconfirmed: The last update (to {to}) is not confirmed yet: run {command} start first and let it confirm or roll back
server-update.restart.dropped: {busy} started after the confirmation: the restart now was cancelled; if you still want it, look at the new list and confirm again
server-update.restart.noRunner: No Runner runs in this process; it cannot be restarted
server-update.restart.notSelfStarting: After exiting this process does not come back by itself
server-update.restart.notSupervised: This process is not a service (it runs in the foreground of a terminal or was started by hand): after exiting it does not come back by itself, so it cannot be restarted from here; stop it in the terminal and start it again (a background process started by {command} start restarts itself)
server-update.restart.selfRestartOff: Restarting itself is turned off (runner.json selfRestart: false or DAISY_RUNNER_SELF_RESTART=0): after exiting it does not come back by itself
server-update.restart.wouldInterrupt: Restarting now would interrupt {busy}; an interrupted turn is marked interrupted and is not redone by itself. Confirm, then ask again (with confirm)
server-update.restart.wouldInterruptAgai: Restarting now would interrupt {busy}; an interrupted turn is marked interrupted and is not redone by itself. New work started after your confirmation: look at the new list and confirm again
server-update.smokeFailed: The new release failed to load: {why}
server-update.source.notAbsolute: A folder or .tgz must be an absolute path; “{path}” is not
server-update.source.notTgz: {path} is neither a folder of .tgz files nor a .tgz file
server-update.source.npmOnly: An npm source can only be {name} (for example {example}); “{spec}” is not
server-update.sourceOff: The update source is turned off (updateSource: off)
server-update.sourceOffUseFrom: The update source is turned off (updateSource: off): name a package with --from <tgz>
server-update.target.olderInstalled: {version} is older than the installed {own}: to go back to an older release add --allow-downgrade
server-update.target.olderRunning: {version} is older than the running {own}: to go back to an older release add --allow-downgrade
server-update.target.sameVersionInstalle: {target} has the same version number as the installed {own} but another build (no telling which is newer): to switch anyway add --allow-downgrade
server-update.target.sameVersionRunning: {target} has the same version number as the running {own} but another build (no telling which is newer): to switch anyway add --allow-downgrade
server-update.wrongOnDisk: After installing, the release on disk is {got}, not {release}
